name: Kraz
description: A star 45 parsecs away, 16 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 61359: radius 15.565 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 160.862 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.049) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 61359: effective temperature 5214 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.037)

gravity.source: SIMBAD's compilation of spectroscopic measurements (mesFe_h): log g 2.85 from 2024A&A...683A.125P; the 16 published values span log g 1.888 to 2.847, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.5% of the centre brightness

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 61359: distance 44.663 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.008), at which the luminosity and radius hold

text.card: A star 45 parsecs away, 16 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 161 times the Sun's luminosity at 5,214 K, so 15.565 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 61359: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Beta Corvi
quotes.card: Beta Corvi is a star in the southern constellation of Corvus.
quotes.introduction: With an apparent visual magnitude of 2.647, it is visible to the naked eye as the second-brightest star in Corvus.

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 3501215734352781440 (quality A), from 2015A&A...574A..50J; Gaia DR3 measures none
